editorial_checks: Keep the Rhine commission's response to a company accident distinct from the international operation implicated in Haiti's harm.
Do not create witnesses, families, quotations, motives, private thoughts or compensation outcomes.
Do not project the 1999 Rhine convention into 1986. Article 11, not Article 9, addresses implementation. Authentic-language and English-translation status are disclosed.
The Rhine 70–100% statistic concerns most priority point-source pollutants, with a pre-accident 1985 baseline; no single-programme causal attribution or all-pollution generalization.
Environmental recovery and individual remedies are distinct. NGO participation is not a damages court, but the essay does not infer that every domestic remedy failed.
Haiti's introduction, spread, responsibility, jurisdiction and individual damages are distinguished; contemporaneous knowledge is not replaced with later evidence.
Alston's criticism is not presented as the Secretariat accepting legal responsibility. The 2013 refusal and the 2016 jurisdictional ruling are not merits exoneration.
The 2016 appellate court is not asserted to have found a Section 29 breach. Immunity's functional rationale and alternative-settlement problem are both retained.
An investigation can be part of a channel; an apology and assistance do not automatically complete a victim-initiated merits process.
Haiti's narrative stops at the 2016 new approach. A/71/895 is used retrospectively to confirm 2016 events, not to claim all later implementation is covered.
The research report is a selection aid, not a substitute for fourteen directly linked sources. No new image assets or source PDFs are stored in the repository.
